record.paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
record.original_question: What is the actual low-temperature magnetic-domain structure of pure LiHoF4, an insulating dipolar Ising ferromagnet whose Ho3+ moments order below about 1.53 K along the crystalline c axis, and can experiments verify the predicted rich structure in which the ground-state domains consist of parallel antiferromagnetically aligned sheets whose sizes and possible branching depend on demagnetization effects and sample geometry?

evidence.quote: For LiHoF4, the ground state domain configuration is expected to consist of parallel antiferromagnetically aligned sheets [17, 18, 19]. The size of the domains increases with decreasing demagnetization factor and, in the limit of infinitely long thin samples, a state of uniform magnetization is possible.

Also, for thick samples, a branched pattern is predicted in the domain structure for a dipolar Ising ferromagnet [17, 18]. LiHoF4 is an excellent test case for theories of domain formation due to the availability of an accurate microscopic model of the material (see below). It remains an open experimental challenge to verify the nature of the predicted rich domain structure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider LiHoF4, an insulating dipolar Ising ferromagnet in which the Ho3+ magnetic moments order below approximately Tc ≈ 1.53 K, with their easy axis along the crystalline c direction. Treat the system as a three-dimensional lattice of classical Ising dipoles interacting solely via the magnetic dipole–dipole interaction (the long-range, angularly anisotropic interaction U(r) ∝ [1 − 3(ẑ·r̂)^2]/|r|^3 between parallel moments aligned along c).

For a finite macroscopic sample of given shape (and hence demagnetization factor N), the competition between bulk dipolar energy and surface/demagnetization energy is predicted to produce a ground-state domain configuration consisting of parallel sheet-like domains of alternating magnetization (an "antiferromagnetic" stacking of ferromagnetic sheets), whose characteristic width grows as N decreases, with a uniformly magnetized state attained in the limit of an infinitely long, thin sample. For sufficiently thick samples, the predicted optimal pattern develops a hierarchical branching structure near the sample surfaces.

Problem: Determine experimentally the actual low-temperature magnetic-domain structure of pure LiHoF4 as a function of sample geometry and demagnetization factor, and verify (or refute) the predicted features: (i) the existence of parallel antiferromagnetically stacked sheet domains in the ordered phase, (ii) the predicted dependence of domain width on demagnetization factor, and (iii) the appearance of a branched domain pattern in thick samples.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent experiments have made significant progress: scanning Hall-probe microscopy below 40 mK (Biltmo & Henelius / Kjäll et al. type studies, and later imaging works) directly observed a multi-domain state in LiHoF4 with parallel/cylinder-like domains a few microns wide, and a 2022 Nature paper reported emergent mesoscale antiferromagnetism near the quantum critical point. These confirm the qualitative picture of antiferromagnetically stacked sheet/cylinder domains and shape dependence, but full quantitative verification of the predicted branched pattern in thick samples and detailed N-dependence of the domain width remains incomplete, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The ferromagnetic transition and domain structure in LiHoF4
status_evidence.snippet: Study of the ferromagnetic transition and domain structure in LiHoF4.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical/experimental analysis of LiHoF4 domain structure with sheet-like domains.

status_evidence.title: SHPM imaging of LiHoF4 at ultra low temperatures
status_evidence.snippet: Domain structure and topography of LiHoF4 were imaged simultaneously below 40 mK using a scanning Hall probe microscope.
status_evidence.claim: Direct imaging of LiHoF4 domains has been performed.

status_evidence.title: Emergence of mesoscale quantum phase transitions in a ferromagnet
status_evidence.snippet: Multi-domain state with emergent mesoscale antiferromagnetism near the quantum critical point in LiHoF4.
status_evidence.claim: Recent experimental work confirms antiferromagnetically arranged ferromagnetic domains.
